title: Usage Credits and Quota Assignment Guidelines for Hosted Inference (2026)
author: Maya Chen
summary: This document defines the recommended model for assigning usage credits and per-route quotas for Redwood's Hosted API. It covers conversion rules, quota types, enforcement windows, migration steps for existing customers, and examples to ensure predictable cost and predictable capacity for product teams.
body:
Overview:
This page describes a prescriptive set of rules and operational procedures for assigning, converting, and enforcing usage credits and per-route quotas for the Redwood Hosted inference product. The goal is to reduce billing surprises for customers while preserving predictable capacity behavior under variable workloads.

Why this matters:
- Customers want clear, auditable rules that explain how API calls map to billable units and to runtime capacity quotas.
- Support and sales need a deterministic conversion matrix when upgrading customers between plans or when granting promotional credits.
- The platform needs consistent enforcement semantics to avoid noisy neighbor incidents and to honor SLAs for tiered customers.

Goals:
1) Produce an unambiguous conversion matrix between API actions (generations, embeddings, streaming tokens) and credit consumption.
2) Define quota types (monthly budget credits, per-minute concurrency, rolling 24h burst allowances) and enforcement windows.
3) Provide a migration plan for customers on legacy "token-minute" pricing to the new credit model.
4) Provide operational runbook steps for support to troubleshoot quota issues.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not prescribe enterprise reserved-capacity contracts for Dedicated or Private deployments (covered separately).
- Not a replacement for the legal Terms — only operational guidance for product and support teams.

Core concepts and definitions:
- Credit unit (CR): the atomic billing unit for Hosted. All billable operations are expressed in CR.
- Request-class: {generation, chat, embedding, rerank, classification}. Each class has a per-token and per-request cost profile.
- Quota bucket: an enforceable allowance attached to an API key or account. Buckets are of three kinds: monthly_budget, concurrency, and burst_pool.
- Burst pool: a rolling window credit allotment (24h) intended to absorb unexpected traffic spikes without immediate hard-throttling.

Conversion matrix (high level):
| Request-class | Metric consumed | Baseline CR rate | Notes |
|---------------|-----------------|------------------|-------|
| Generation | output_tokens + prompt_weighted_input_tokens | 1.0 CR per 1k output tokens + 0.4 CR per 1k input tokens | Streaming prorated per token as emitted |
| Chat | message_tokens + context_window_amortized | 1.2 CR per 1k tokens | System messages treated as input at 0.4 CR/1k |
| Embedding | vector_units | 0.25 CR per 1k tokens equivalent | Small fixed cost floor of 0.01 CR to prevent zero-cost queries |
| Rerank | candidate_eval_units | 0.6 CR per candidate per 1k tokens | Multiply by #candidates |

Note: the matrix above is normative for assigning credits during billing cycles. Quantization and optimized kernels may reduce actual backend resource consumption; platform adjusts cost multipliers quarterly and documents changes in pricing-change-notices.

Quota types and enforcement semantics:
1) monthly_budget (hard): A monthly CR cap. When exhausted, requests receive HTTP 402 (Payment Required) with body code "quota_exceeded.monthly_budget" unless account configured for auto-topup.
2) concurrency (soft then hard): A per-account concurrent request cap measured over 1s windows. Soft limit issues 429 with header X-Quota-Action: slow-down and offers Retry-After. If soft limit persists for >10s, platform escalates to hard 429 with X-Quota-Blocked.
3) burst_pool (grace): Rolling 24h pool that replenishes linearly. When monthly_budget is near exhaustion, burst_pool provides allowance up to configured percentage of monthly_budget. Exhausting both results in hard-block.

Enforcement flow (simple):
1) Request arrives.
2) Charge estimated CR from burst_pool or monthly_budget based on current state.
3) If estimated charge exceeds available in both buckets, return block response with suggested remedial steps.
4) After request completes, reconcile actual CR consumed and adjust buckets; if actual > estimated, reconciliation can result in negative-balance grace (up to 5% of monthly_budget) before hard-block.

Migration story for legacy customers (timeline & steps):
- Objective: Migrate customers currently on the "token-minute" plans to CR model with minimal disruption and clear audit trail.
- Migration window: Q1 2026 (target).
- Steps: 1) Export legacy usage logs and compute equivalent CR using the Conversion matrix (generate per-account migration report). 2) Apply one-time migration credit equal to the account's trailing-3-month median monthly consumption + 10% buffer. 3) Flag accounts for manual review if trailing usage shows >3x variance month-to-month. 4) Notify customers 30 days in advance with migration report and sandboxed preview of post-migration invoice.

Edge cases and dispute handling:
- If a customer disputes the conversion, provide the per-request audit log (request-id, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_CR, reconciled_CR) for the disputed billing period. Support may apply a refund credit up to 100% for systemic conversion errors discovered by finance.
- For customers with high variance, recommend Dedicated or reserved capacity rather than extending larger burst pools.

Operational runbook (support-facing quick steps):
1) When a customer reports "quota exceeded":
   a) Ask for request-id or approximate timestamp and route.
   b) Check per-account bucket state in Admin Console -> Usage -> Buckets.
   c) Pull request audit log and reconcile estimated vs actual CR.
   d) If reconciliation shows a platform bug (e.g., double-counting on retry), escalate to Billing and Runtime teams with label: billing-incident.
   e) For legitimate overages, offer one-time courtesy credit following the Customer Help Credit policy (max $X for Starter, $Y for Growth).
2) When a customer needs temporary capacity increase:
   a) For scheduled events, follow Capacity Ramp procedure: create scheduled uplift in Gateway config, set provisional burst_pool percentage, and create Support ticket with capacity window.
   b) For emergency spikes, consider temporary auto-topup if account has payment method on file.

Metrics and telemetry to surface:
- Daily consumed CR per account and per-route.
- Fraction of requests consuming burst_pool vs monthly_budget.
- Incidents where reconciliation delta > 2% (indicator of metering issues).
- Customer-visible latency change after quota throttling events.

SLOs (product-facing):
- Billing accuracy: 99.5% of reconciled charges should be within 2% of estimated charges per account per month.
- Quota enforcement latency: enforcement decisions (charge/allow/block) must be returned within 50ms for 99th percentile of requests.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 (internal pilot, Jan 2026): implement conversion engine in staging and run shadow billing for 50 pilot customers.
Phase 1 (beta, Feb 2026): enable migration preview for top 500 customers and accept opt-in.
Phase 2 (GA, Apr 2026): full roll-out to new accounts and migration invitations by queue; legacy accounts scheduled by risk tier.

Appendix A — Example conversions and JSON snippet:
Example: user calls chat endpoint with 2 system messages (50 tokens each), 3 user messages (avg 80 tokens), model returns 400 tokens:
- Input_tokens = 50*2 + 80*3 = 310
- Output_tokens = 400
- Estimated CR = (400 / 1000 * 1.2) + (310 / 1000 * 0.4) = 0.48 + 0.124 = 0.604 CR

Migration report JSON (example):
{
  "account_id": "acct_123",
  "legacy_avg_monthly_token_minutes": "1,200,000",
  "computed_monthly_CR_equivalent": "720",
  "migration_credit_grant": "792"  // 10% buffer
}

Appendix B — Frequently asked questions:
Q: Will burst_pool increase my bill?
A: No. The billing charge still consumes monthly_budget CR; burst_pool is only an elasticity mechanism to avoid immediate blocking. Customers exceeding monthly_budget will still be charged for CR consumed unless they opt for reserved capacity.

Q: How often will conversion multipliers change?
A: We plan quarterly adjustments tied to runtime efficiency improvements. Any multiplier change will be communicated with a 60-day notice and accompanied by a migration table for historical data.
